ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, on the left side there is a voltage source V_{o2}, whose upper end is connected through a resistor R to the contact “2” of the switch SW. In the middle there is a voltage source V_{o1}, whose upper end is connected to the switch contact “1”. The common end of the switch is connected to the right-side branch; the right-side branch first passes through a resistor R, and then is connected to the upper end of capacitor C; the lower end of the capacitor and the lower ends of the two voltage sources share the same reference node. The capacitor voltage v_c is marked across the two ends of the capacitor, with direction being the upper end relative to the lower end. Reasoning: When the switch remains at position 1 for a long time, the capacitor reaches DC steady state, and there is no DC current in the capacitor branch, so there is no voltage drop across the right-side resistor R, and the voltage at the upper end of the capacitor equals V_{o1}. So v_c(0^-)=V_{o1}. The capacitor voltage cannot change abruptly, therefore v_c(0^+)=V_{o1}. When t>0, the switch moves to position 2, and the capacitor is connected to V_{o2} through the right-side resistor R, the switch, and the left-side resistor R. Looking in from the capacitor terminal, when open-circuited there is no current, and there is no voltage drop across the two resistors, so the Thevenin voltage V_{th}=V_{o2}; after setting the independent voltage source V_{o2} to zero, the capacitor terminal to ground passes through two series resistors, so R_{th}=2R. Therefore the first-order RC response is v_c(t)=V_{th}+[v_c(0^+)-V_{th}]e^{-t/(R_{th}C)}=V_{o2}+(V_{o1}-V_{o2})e^{-t/(2RC)}, equivalently written as (V_{o2}-V_{o1})(1-e^{-t/(2RC)})+V_{o1}.

Looking in from the capacitor terminal, when open-circuited there is no current, and there is no voltage drop across the two resistors, so the Thevenin voltage V_{th}=V_{o2}; after setting the independent voltage source V_{o2} to zero, the capacitor terminal to ground passes through two series resistors, so R_{th}=2R. Therefore the first-order RC response is v_c(t)=V_{th}+[v_c(0^+)-V_{th}]e^{-t/(R_{th}C)}=V_{o2}+(V_{o1}-V_{o2})e^{-t/(2RC)}, equivalently written as (V_{o2}-V_{o1})(1-e^{-t/(2RC)})+V_{o1}.
